records.text: On June 18, Bret Weinstein had a text exchange with Charlie Kirk, who said he was spending two full days at the White House trying to persuade President Trump not to initiate war with Iran.
records.speaker: Bret Weinstein

appearances.snippet: Brett (Brett Weinstein) opens this up. By saying on June 18th, I had a text exchange with Charlie Kirk. He said he was spending two full days at the White House trying to persuade President Trump (Donald J. Trump) not to initiate a war with Iran.

verification.notes: Transcript context at 11:05 identifies a quoted Bret Weinstein post. Weinstein's public post states that on June 18 he exchanged texts with Charlie Kirk and that Kirk said he was spending two days at the White House opposing war with Iran. This verifies the quoted-post conveyance; the private exchange and White House attendance are supported by the posted screenshot/account but not independently authenticated.

sources.title: Bret Weinstein post about his June 18 exchange with Charlie Kirk
sources.relevance: Primary public post containing the quoted account of the exchange and two White House days.

records.text: It is reasonable to wonder whether Charlie Kirk's refusal to back down from opposing war with Iran somehow resulted in his murder.
records.speaker: Bret Weinstein

appearances.snippet: Given that Charlie (Charlie Kirk) was close with the president and that he represented a large constituency essential to Trump (Donald J. Trump), and given that many proponents of the war with Iran saw a U.S. attack as urgently necessary to the survival of Israel, it is reasonable to wonder if his refusal to back down from his steadfast opposition somehow resulted in his murder.

verification.notes: Transcript context at 11:17 accurately quotes Bret Weinstein's public post. The source uses the qualifier 'reasonable to wonder' and poses a causal question rather than asserting that opposition to war caused Kirk's murder. Verification is of the quoted post and its qualified wording, not proof of the suggested theory.

sources.title: Bret Weinstein post about Charlie Kirk and the Iran war
sources.relevance: Primary public post containing the qualified 'reasonable to wonder' language quoted in the episode.

records.text: Candace Owens said Tucker Carlson, Bret Weinstein, and Joe Kent had all confirmed that Charlie Kirk was fighting behind the scenes to stop a war with Iran.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Frank Turek—somebody was full of it. I'm sorry. Um, Ali (commenter; surname unverified) writes, 'Have you seen the clip where Erika says, We don't know how Charlie would feel about the Iran war?' Yeah, I saw that. That deserves way more outrage. Tucker (Tucker Carlson), Bret Weinstein, Joe (Joe Kent) have all confirmed that he was fighting hard behind the scenes to stop it. What a betrayal. It's just what Erika (Erika Kirk) is—what she is. She's reversed course on everything, everything that Charlie (Charlie Kirk) believed. I believe she had more loyalty to people that brought her in—

verification.notes: Transcript audit and live-source comparison show the third name is Joe Kent, not Joe Rogan; the statement text/entity reference was corrected through the statements helper. Tucker Carlson described discussing anti-Iran-war concerns with Kirk, Bret Weinstein published a June 18 exchange in which Kirk said he was spending two days at the White House trying to prevent war, and Joe Kent recounted Kirk directly urging him to stop a war with Iran. The three attributed confirmations are supported.
